newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker with U.S. issues.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker with U.S. issues.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened slightly weaker on Monday, matching losses in U.S. Treasuries, with some investors selling to lock in gains after four consecutive sessions of strong gains last week, analysts said.

"You could identify a little bit of profit-taking here after what happened last week, not to a very large scale, but I think that's the major thing that's going on right now," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.27 to C$110.90 to yield 7.077 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 7/32 to yield 6.89 percent. The spread between the two bonds was 19 basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets saw sharp gains last week, with the Canadian market closing stronger for four out of five sessions. Canadian and U.S. bonds rallied amid economic reports which reduced expectations of tightening by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
"I would say that after the kind of run that we had last week we were probably due to consolidate a little bit," said TD's Webber.

Webber said Canadian markets are likely to trade in a sideways fashion for the early part of this week amid a lack of significant U.S. economic data. Analysts said Canadian economic reports out this morning on foreign reserves and building permits had little to no impact on bonds.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bonds fell C$0.17 to C$103.33 to yield 6.526 percent. The U.S. bond fell 7/32 to yield 6.68 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was 15 basis points, unchanged from Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.02 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.22 percent.
